title: Meter the quote source without breaking its batch request

blocks.text: The pricing page shows a few dozen stock quotes and asks for them with one `quoteAll(...)` call. The remote quote service answers a whole list in one request. Last week a `Metered` decorator went in front of it, so the dashboard can show how many symbols are quoted, and since then the quote service's request count has jumped and its rate limit trips at lunchtime.

Finish `Metered.quoteAll(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/QuoteMetrics.java`: a page must still cost the remote service one request, and the dashboard must count every symbol quoted, whether it was asked for alone or as part of a page. About two lines in total.

cases.says: quoteAll through the decorator returns a quote for every symbol, in the order asked
a page quoted through the decorator reaches the remote service as one request, its own batch call
symbols quoted through quoteAll are counted, not only those quoted one at a time
the count is the number of symbols quoted, not the number of calls

origin.section: A Decorator That Doesn't Override a Default Method Runs the Interface's Code, Not the Wrapped Object's

concepts: A default method the decorator doesn't override runs the interface's code on the decorator, so the wrapped object's override, such as an atomic computeIfAbsent or a batch call, is never reached.
Overriding the default to forward straight to the wrapped object keeps its behaviour but skips the decorator's own work, so the override must forward and decorate.
